objectives.label: Sample space and probability
objectives.description: Write the sample space and events of a random experiment as sets and calculate the probability P(A) = n(A)/n(S).

objectives.label: Intersection and mutually exclusive
objectives.description: Determine the intersection A ∩ B of two events using a Venn diagram, calculate its probability, and identify mutually exclusive events.

objectives.label: Union of events
objectives.description: Determine the union A ∪ B of two events and calculate its probability using P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B), including for mutually exclusive events.

passages.text: A regular dice is rolled once randomly and the upper face is observed as :

A.why: A dice rolled once and the upper face observed is a random experiment a student can picture, setting up sample space and probability.

B.why: Rolling a regular dice once and observing the upper face is a picturable situation that motivates sample space and probability.

A.why: A side note that probability can be written as a fraction or percentage, with no motivating situation or reflection.

B.why: A side note restating that probability can be written as a fraction or percentage.

passages.text: Events are subset of the sample space (S), so oparetions on events are similar to the operations on sets such as union and intersection. When the sample sapce (S) is considered the universal set, we can represent events and operations on the sample space by using Venn diagrams:

A.why: The book says events are subsets of S so operations on events are like set operations, shown with Venn diagrams, which introduces the lesson's ideas as a whole.

B.why: Explains that events are subsets of the sample space so operations on sets apply, introducing the lesson's idea with no worked numbers.

passages.text: Notic that A and B are mutually exclusive events. Then P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B) but (A ∩ B) = zero. ∴ P(A ∪ B) = 4/9 + 1/9 - zero = 5/9 As previously found

A.why: A worked step applying the union formula to mutually exclusive events with numbers, not an introduction or reflection.

B.why: A step of a worked solution applying the union formula for mutually exclusive events.

lessons.title: Complementary event and the difference between two events

objectives.label: Complementary event and its probability
objectives.description: Determine the complementary event A` of an event A in a sample space S (A ∪ A` = S, A ∩ A` = φ) and calculate P(A`) using P(A`) = 1 - P(A).

objectives.label: Difference between two events
objectives.description: Calculate the probability of the difference between two events, A - B (the occurrence of A only), from set counts or a Venn diagram, using (A - B) ∪ (A ∩ B) = A.

passages.text: In the venn diagram opposite: If S is the universal set, A ⊂ S then the complementary set of A is A`.

A.why: The book introduces what a complementary set A` is in a universal set S, with no worked numbers.

B.why: The book introduces what the complementary set A` is, using a Venn diagram and no numbers.

passages.text: From the previous, we notice that: If S is the sample space of a random experiment and one ball is drawn from a box having identical balls numbered from 1 to 7 and observing the number on it. A is the event of getting even number: A = {2, 4, 6}. A` is the event of getting an odd number: A` = {1, 3, 5, 7} and it is a complementary event to A.

A.why: A ball drawn from a box of numbered balls (even vs odd) is a pictureable situation showing a complementary event.

B.why: It is a worked example of finding A` for the numbers 1 to 7.

passages.text: From the previous table, notice that: P (A) + P (A`) = 1 then: P (A`) = 1 - P (A), P (A) = 1 - P (A`)

A.why: It restates the formula P(A`) = 1 - P(A) after a table, not an introduction.

B.why: It restates the formula P(A`) = 1 - P(A) after the table.

passages.text: Does the event reading Al Akhbar newspaper mean to read Al Akhbar newspaper only? Explain your answer.

A.why: Reading a newspaper versus reading it only is an everyday situation that motivates the difference of two events.

B.why: It is a question that asks the student to explain an answer, not a framing or a look back.

passages.text: Notice that: The event of reading Al Akhbar newspaper is represented by venn opposite diagram by set A while the event of reading Al Akhbar only but not other newspaper is represented by the set A - B

A.why: It explains what the set A - B means (reading Al Akhbar only) using a Venn diagram, without worked numbers.

B.why: The book explains what A - B means: reading Al Akhbar only, as opposed to the whole set A.
